verses.zh: 大卫王年纪老迈，虽用被遮盖，仍不觉暖。
verses.en: King David was very old;[NOTE:1] even when they covered him with blankets,[NOTE:2] he could not get warm.
notes: Heb “was old, coming into the days” (i.e., advancing in years).
Or “garments.”

verses.zh: 所以臣仆对他说：「不如为我主我王寻找一个处女，使她伺候王，奉养王，睡在王的怀中，好叫我主我王得暖。」
verses.en: His servants advised[NOTE:1] him, “A young virgin must be found for our master, the king,[NOTE:2] to take care of the king’s needs[NOTE:3] and serve as his nurse. She can also sleep with you[NOTE:4] and keep our master, the king, warm.”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “said to.”

Heb “let them seek for my master, the king, a young girl, a virgin.” The third person plural subject of the verb is indefinite (see GKC 460 §144.f). The appositional expression, “a young girl, a virgin,” is idiomatic; the second term specifically defines the more general first term (see IBHS 230 §12.3b).
Heb “and she will stand before the king.” The Hebrew phrase “stand before” can mean “to attend; to serve” (BDB 764 s.v. עָמַד).

Heb “and she will lie down in your bosom.” The expression might imply sexual intimacy (see 2 Sam 12:3 [where the lamb symbolizes Bathsheba] and Mic 7:5), though v. 4b indicates that David did not actually have sex with the young woman.
Heb “and my master, the king, will be warm.”

verses.zh: 于是在以色列全境寻找美貌的童女，寻得书念的一个童女亚比煞，就带到王那里。
verses.en: So they looked through all Israel[NOTE:1] for a beautiful young woman and found Abishag, a Shunammite, and brought her to the king.
notes: Heb “through all the territory of Israel.”

verses.zh: 这童女极其美貌，她奉养王，伺候王，王却没有与她亲近。
verses.en: The young woman was very beautiful; she became the king’s nurse and served him, but the king was not intimate with her.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “did not know her.” The verb יָדַע (yadaʿ, “to know”) is a euphemism for sexual relations.

verses.zh: 那时，哈及的儿子亚多尼雅自尊，说：「我必作王」，就为自己预备车辆、马兵，又派五十人在他前头奔走。
verses.en: Now Adonijah, son of David and Haggith,[NOTE:1] was promoting himself,[NOTE:2] boasting,[NOTE:3] “I will be king!” He managed to acquire[NOTE:4] chariots and horsemen, as well as 50 men to serve as his royal guard.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “son of Haggith,” but since this formula usually designates the father (who in this case was David), the translation specifies that David was Adonijah’s father.sn Haggith was one of David’s wives (2 Sam 3:4; 2 Chr 3:2).
Heb “lifting himself up.”
Heb “saying.”
Or “he acquired for himself.”
Heb “to run ahead of him.”

verses.zh: 他父亲素来没有使他忧闷，说：「你是做甚么呢？」他甚俊美，生在押沙龙之后。
verses.en: (Now his father had never corrected[NOTE:1] him[NOTE:2] by saying, “Why do you do such things?” He was also very handsome and had been born right after Absalom.[NOTE:3])
notes: Or “disciplined.”
Heb “did not correct him from his days.” The phrase “from his days” means “from his earliest days,” or “ever in his life.” See GKC 382 §119.w, n. 2.
Heb “and she gave birth to him after Absalom.” This does not imply they had the same mother; Absalom’s mother was Maacah, not Haggith (2 Sam 3:4).

verses.zh: 亚多尼雅与洗鲁雅的儿子约押，和祭司亚比亚他商议；二人就顺从他，帮助他。
verses.en: He collaborated[NOTE:1] with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they supported[NOTE:2] him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his words were.”
Heb “helped after” (i.e., stood by).
Heb “Adonijah.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“him”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 但祭司撒督、耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅、先知拿单、示每、利以，并大卫的勇士都不顺从亚多尼雅。
verses.en: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s elite warriors[NOTE:1] did not ally themselves[NOTE:2] with Adonijah.
notes: Or “bodyguard” (Heb “mighty men”).
Heb “were not.”

verses.zh: 一日，亚多尼雅在隐・罗结旁、琐希列磐石那里宰了牛羊、肥犊，请他的诸弟兄，就是王的众子，并所有作王臣仆的犹大人；
verses.en: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened steers at the Stone of Zoheleth near En Rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king’s sons,[NOTE:1] as well as all the men of Judah, the king’s servants.
notes: The ancient Greek version omits this appositional phrase.

verses.zh: 惟独先知拿单和比拿雅并勇士，与他的兄弟所罗门，他都没有请。
verses.en: But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the elite warriors,[NOTE:1] or his brother Solomon.
notes: Or “bodyguard” (Heb “mighty men”).

verses.zh: 拿单对所罗门的母亲拔示巴说：「哈及的儿子亚多尼雅作王了，你没有听见吗？我们的主大卫却不知道。
verses.en: Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, “Has it been reported to you[NOTE:1] that Haggith’s son Adonijah has become king behind our master David’s back?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Have you not heard?”
Heb “and our master David does not know.”

verses.zh: 现在我可以给你出个主意，好保全你和你儿子所罗门的性命。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] let me give you some advice as to how[NOTE:2] you can save your life and your son Solomon’s life.
notes: Heb “now, come.” The imperative of הָלַךְ (halakh) is here used as an introductory interjection. See BDB 234 s.v. חָלַךְ.
Or “so that.”

verses.zh: 你进去见大卫王，对他说：『我主我王啊，你不曾向婢女起誓说：你儿子所罗门必接续我作王，坐在我的位上吗？现在亚多尼雅怎么作了王呢？』
verses.en: Visit[NOTE:1] King David and say to him, ‘My master, O king, did you not solemnly promise[NOTE:2] your servant, “Surely your son Solomon will be king after me; he will sit on my throne”? So why has Adonijah become king?’
notes: Heb “come, go to.” The imperative of הָלַךְ (halakh) is here used as an introductory interjection. See BDB 234 s.v. חָלַךְ.
Or “swear an oath to.”

verses.zh: 你还与王说话的时候，我也随后进去，证实你的话。」
verses.en: While[NOTE:1] you are still there speaking to the king, I will arrive[NOTE:2] and verify your report.”[NOTE:3]
notes: In the Hebrew text the sentence is introduced by the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh, “look”), which here draws attention to Nathan’s concluding word of assurance and support. For this use of the word, see HALOT 252 s.v. הִנֵּה.
The Hebrew text reads, “I will come after you.”
Heb “fill up [i.e., confirm] your words.”

verses.zh: 拔示巴进入内室见王，王甚老迈，书念的童女亚比煞正伺候王。
verses.en: So Bathsheba visited the king in his private quarters.[NOTE:1] (The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.)
notes: Or “bedroom.”

verses.zh: 拔示巴向王屈身下拜；王说：「你要甚么？」
verses.en: Bathsheba bowed down on the floor before[NOTE:1] the king. The king said, “What do you want?”
notes: Heb “bowed low and bowed down to.”

verses.zh: 她说：「我主啊，你曾向婢女指着耶和华―你的　神起誓说：『你儿子所罗门必接续我作王，坐在我的位上。』
verses.en: She replied to him, “My master, you swore an oath to your servant by the Lord your God, ‘Solomon your son will be king after me and he will sit on my throne.’

verses.zh: 现在亚多尼雅作王了，我主我王却不知道。
verses.en: But now, look, Adonijah has become king! But you,[NOTE:1] my master the king, are not even aware of it![NOTE:2]
notes: Instead of עַתָּה (ʿattah, “now”) many Hebrew mss, along with the Old Greek, Syriac Peshitta, and Latin Vulgate, have the similar sounding independent pronoun אַתָּה (ʾattah, “you”). This reading is followed in the present translation.
Heb “you do not know [about it].”

verses.zh: 他宰了许多牛羊、肥犊，请了王的众子和祭司亚比亚他，并元帅约押；惟独王的仆人所罗门，他没有请。
verses.en: He has sacrificed many cattle, steers, and sheep and has invited all the king’s sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab, the commander of the army, but he has not invited your servant Solomon.

verses.zh: 我主我王啊，以色列众人的眼目都仰望你，等你晓谕他们，在我主我王之后谁坐你的位。
verses.en: Now,[NOTE:1] my master, O king, all Israel is watching anxiously to see who is named to succeed my master the king on the throne.[NOTE:2]
notes: Many Hebrew mss have עַתָּה (ʿattah, “now”) rather than the similar sounding independent pronoun אַתָּה (ʾattah, “you”).
Heb “the eyes of all Israel are upon you to declare to them who will sit on the throne of my master the king after him.”

verses.zh: 若不然，到我主我王与列祖同睡以后，我和我儿子所罗门必算为罪人了。」
verses.en: If a decision is not made,[NOTE:1] when my master the king is buried with his ancestors,[NOTE:2] my son Solomon and I[NOTE:3] will be considered state criminals.”[NOTE:4]
notes: The words “if a decision is not made” are added for clarification.
Heb “lies down with his fathers.”
Heb “I and my son Solomon.” The order has been reversed in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “will be guilty”; NASB “considered offenders”; TEV “treated as traitors.”

verses.zh: 拔示巴还与王说话的时候，先知拿单也进来了。
verses.en: Just then,[NOTE:1] while she was still speaking to the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
notes: Heb “look.” The particle הִנֵּה (hinneh) here draws attention to Nathan’s arrival and invites the audience to view the scene through the eyes of the participants.

verses.zh: 有人奏告王说：「先知拿单来了。」拿单进到王前，脸伏于地。
verses.en: The king was told, “Nathan the prophet is here.” Nathan entered and bowed before the king with his face to the floor.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “ground.” Since this was indoors, “floor” is more appropriate than “ground.”

verses.zh: 拿单说：「我主我王果然应许亚多尼雅说『你必接续我作王，坐在我的位上』吗？
verses.en: Nathan said, “My master, O king, did you announce, ‘Adonijah will be king after me; he will sit on my throne’?

verses.zh: 他今日下去，宰了许多牛羊、肥犊，请了王的众子和军长，并祭司亚比亚他；他们正在亚多尼雅面前吃喝，说：『愿亚多尼雅王万岁！』
verses.en: For today he has gone down and sacrificed many cattle, steers, and sheep and has invited all the king’s sons, the army commanders, and Abiathar the priest. At this moment[NOTE:1] they are having a feast[NOTE:2] in his presence, and they have declared, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “look.”
Heb “eating and drinking.”
Heb “let the king, Adonijah, live!”

verses.zh: 惟独我，就是你的仆人和祭司撒督，耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，并王的仆人所罗门，他都没有请。
verses.en: But he did not invite me—your servant—or Zadok the priest, or Benaiah son of Jehoiada, or your servant Solomon.

verses.zh: 这事果然出乎我主我王吗？王却没有告诉仆人们，在我主我王之后谁坐你的位。」
verses.en: Has my master the king authorized this without informing your servants[NOTE:1] who should succeed my master the king on his throne?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Many Hebrew mss and ancient textual witnesses agree with the Qere in reading this as singular, “your servant.”
Heb “From my master the king is this thing done, and you did not make known to your servants who will sit on the throne of my master the king after him?”

verses.zh: 大卫王吩咐说：「叫拔示巴来。」拔示巴就进来，站在王面前。
verses.en: King David responded,[NOTE:1] “Summon Bathsheba!”[NOTE:2] She came and stood before the king.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “answered and said.”
Summon Bathsheba. Bathsheba must have left the room when Nathan arrived (see 1:22).
Heb “she came before the king and stood before the king.”

verses.zh: 王起誓说：「我指着救我性命脱离一切苦难、永生的耶和华起誓。
verses.en: The king swore an oath: “As certainly as the Lord lives (he who has rescued me[NOTE:1] from every danger),
notes: Or “ransomed my life.”

verses.zh: 我既然指着耶和华―以色列的　神向你起誓说：你儿子所罗门必接续我作王，坐在我的位上。我今日就必照这话而行。」
verses.en: I will keep[NOTE:1] today the oath I swore to you by the Lord God of Israel: ‘Surely Solomon your son will be king after me; he will sit in my place on my throne.’”
notes: Or “carry out, perform.”

verses.zh: 于是，拔示巴脸伏于地，向王下拜，说：「愿我主大卫王万岁！」
verses.en: Bathsheba bowed down to the king with her face to the floor[NOTE:1] and said, “May my master, King David, live forever!”
notes: Heb “bowed low, face [to] the ground, and bowed down to the king.”

verses.zh: 大卫王又吩咐说：「将祭司撒督、先知拿单、耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅召来！」他们就都来到王面前。
verses.en: King David said, “Summon Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet,[NOTE:1] and Benaiah son of Jehoiada.” They came before the king,
notes: Summon…Nathan. Nathan must have left the room when Bathsheba reentered.

verses.zh: 王对他们说：「要带领你们主的仆人，使我儿子所罗门骑我的骡子，送他下到基训；
verses.en: and he[NOTE:1] told them, “Take your master’s[NOTE:2] servants with you, put my son Solomon on my mule, and lead him down to Gihon.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the king.”
The plural form is used in the Hebrew text to indicate honor and authority.
Heb “mount Solomon my son on the mule that belongs to me and take him down to Gihon.”

verses.zh: 在那里，祭司撒督和先知拿单要膏他作以色列的王；你们也要吹角，说：『愿所罗门王万岁！』
verses.en: There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet will anoint[NOTE:1] him king over Israel; then blow the trumpet and declare, ‘Long live King Solomon!’
notes: Or “designate” (i.e., by anointing with oil).

verses.zh: 然后要跟随他上来，使他坐在我的位上，接续我作王。我已立他作以色列和犹大的君。」
verses.en: Then follow him up as he comes and sits on my throne. He will be king in my place; I have decreed[NOTE:1] that he will be ruler over Israel and Judah.”
notes: Or “commanded.”

verses.zh: 耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅对王说：「阿们！愿耶和华―我主我王的　神也这样命定。
verses.en: Benaiah son of Jehoiada responded[NOTE:1] to the king: “So be it![NOTE:2] May the Lord God of my master the king confirm it![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “answered and said.”
Or “Amen.”
Heb “So may the Lord God of my master the king say.”

verses.zh: 耶和华怎样与我主我王同在，愿他照样与所罗门同在，使他的国位比我主大卫王的国位更大。」
verses.en: As the Lord is with my master the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he make him an even greater king than my master King David!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my master King David.”

verses.zh: 于是，祭司撒督、先知拿单、耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，和基利提人、比利提人都下去使所罗门骑大卫王的骡子，将他送到基训。
verses.en: So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites, and the Pelethites[NOTE:1] went down, put Solomon on King David’s mule, and led him to Gihon.
notes: The Kerethites and Pelethites were members of David’s royal guard (see 2 Sam 8:18). The Kerethites may have been descendants of an ethnic group originating in Crete.

verses.zh: 祭司撒督就从帐幕中取了盛膏油的角来，用膏膏所罗门。人就吹角，众民都说：「愿所罗门王万岁！」
verses.en: Zadok the priest took a horn filled with olive oil[NOTE:1] from the tent and poured it on[NOTE:2] Solomon; the trumpet was blown and all the people declared, “Long live King Solomon!”
notes: A horn filled with oil. An animal’s horn was used as an oil flask in the anointing ceremony.tn Heb “the horn of oil.” This has been specified as olive oil in the translation for clarity.
Or “anointed.”

verses.zh: 众民跟随他上来，且吹笛，大大欢呼，声音震地。
verses.en: All the people followed him up, playing flutes and celebrating so loudly they made the ground shake.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and all the people went up after him, and the people were playing flutes and rejoicing with great joy and the ground split open at the sound of them.” The verb בָּקַע (baqaʿ, “to split open”), which elsewhere describes the effects of an earthquake, is obviously here an exaggeration for the sake of emphasis.

verses.zh: 亚多尼雅和所请的众客筵宴方毕，听见这声音；约押听见角声就说：「城中为何有这响声呢？」
verses.en: Now Adonijah and all his guests heard the commotion just as they had finished eating.[NOTE:1] When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he asked, “Why is there such a noisy commotion in the city?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard, now they had finished eating.”
Heb “Why is the city’s sound noisy?”

verses.zh: 他正说话的时候，祭司亚比亚他的儿子约拿单来了。亚多尼雅对他说：「进来吧！你是个忠义的人，必是报好信息。」
verses.en: As he was still speaking, Jonathan[NOTE:1] son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said, “Come in, for[NOTE:2] an important man like you must be bringing good news.”[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew text has “look” at this point. The particle הִנֵּה (hinneh), “look” draws attention to Jonathan’s arrival and invites the audience to view the scene through the eyes of the participants.
Or “surely.”

Heb “you are a man of strength [or “ability”] and you bring a message [that is] good.” Another option is to understand the phrase אִישׁ חַיִל (ʾish khayil) in the sense of “a worthy man,” that is “loyal.” See also 1 Kgs 1:52 and HALOT 311 s.v. חַיִל.

verses.zh: 约拿单对亚多尼雅说：「我们的主大卫王诚然立所罗门为王了。
verses.en: Jonathan replied[NOTE:1] to Adonijah: “No![NOTE:2] Our master[NOTE:3] King David has made Solomon king.
notes: Heb “answered and said.”
For a similar use of אֲבָל (ʾaval), see Gen 17:19, where God rejects Abraham’s proposal and offers an alternative.
The plural form is used in the Hebrew text to indicate honor and authority.

verses.zh: 王差遣祭司撒督、先知拿单、耶何耶大的儿子比拿雅，和基利提人、比利提人都去使所罗门骑王的骡子。
verses.en: The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites, and the Pelethites and they put him on the king’s mule.

verses.zh: 祭司撒督和先知拿单在基训已经膏他作王。众人都从那里欢呼着上来，声音使城震动，这就是你们所听见的声音；
verses.en: Then Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed[NOTE:1] him king in Gihon. They went up from there rejoicing, and the city is in an uproar. That is the sound you hear.
notes: I.e., designated by anointing with oil.

verses.zh: 并且所罗门登了国位。
verses.en: Furthermore, Solomon has assumed the royal throne.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And also Solomon sits on the throne of the kingdom.”

verses.zh: 王的臣仆也来为我们的主大卫王祝福，说：『愿王的　神使所罗门的名比王的名更尊荣；使他的国位比王的国位更大。』王就在床上屈身下拜。
verses.en: The king’s servants have even come to congratulate[NOTE:1] our master[NOTE:2] King David, saying, ‘May your God[NOTE:3] make Solomon more famous than you and make him an even greater king than you!’[NOTE:4] Then the king leaned[NOTE:5] on the bed
notes: Heb “to bless.”
The plural form is used in the Hebrew text to indicate honor and authority.
Many Hebrew mss agree with the Qere in reading simply “God.”
Heb “make the name of Solomon better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne.” The term שֵׁם (shem, “name”) is used here of one’s fame and reputation.
Or “bowed down; worshiped.”

verses.zh: 王又说：『耶和华―以色列的　神是应当称颂的；因他赐我一人今日坐在我的位上，我也亲眼看见了。』」
verses.en: and said[NOTE:1] this: ‘The Lord God of Israel is worthy of praise because[NOTE:2] today he has placed a successor on my throne and allowed me to see it.’”[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew text reads, “and the king said.”
Or “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who….” In this blessing formula אֲשֶׁר (ʾasher, “who; because”) introduces the reason why the one being blessed deserves the honor.
Heb “and my eyes are seeing.”

verses.zh: 亚多尼雅的众客听见这话就都惊惧，起来四散。
verses.en: All of Adonijah’s guests panicked;[NOTE:1] they jumped up and rushed off their separate ways.
notes: Or “were afraid, trembled.”

verses.zh: 亚多尼雅惧怕所罗门，就起来，去抓住祭坛的角。
verses.en: Adonijah feared Solomon, so he got up and went and grabbed hold of the horns of the altar.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grabbed hold of the horns of the altar. The “horns” of the altar were the horn-shaped projections on the four corners of the altar (see Exod 27:2). By going to the holy place and grabbing hold of the horns of the altar, Adonijah was seeking asylum from Solomon.

verses.zh: 有人告诉所罗门说：「亚多尼雅惧怕所罗门王，现在抓住祭坛的角，说：『愿所罗门王今日向我起誓，必不用刀杀仆人。』」
verses.en: Solomon was told, “Look, Adonijah fears you;[NOTE:1] see, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, ‘May King Solomon solemnly promise[NOTE:2] me today that he will not kill his servant with the sword.’”
notes: Heb “King Solomon.” The name and title have been replaced by the pronoun (“you”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Or “swear an oath to.”

verses.zh: 所罗门说：「他若作忠义的人，连一根头发也不致落在地上；他若行恶，必要死亡。」
verses.en: Solomon said, “If he is a loyal subject,[NOTE:1] not a hair of his head will be harmed, but if he is found to be a traitor,[NOTE:2] he will die.”
notes: Heb “if he is a man of strength [or ability].” In this context, where Adonijah calls himself a “servant,” implying allegiance to the new king, the phrase אִישׁ חַיִל (ʾish khayil) probably carries the sense of “a worthy man,” that is, “loyal” (see HALOT 311 s.v. חַיִל).
Heb “but if evil is found in him.”

verses.zh: 于是所罗门王差遣人，使亚多尼雅从坛上下来，他就来，向所罗门王下拜；所罗门对他说：「你回家去吧！」
verses.en: King Solomon sent men to bring him down[NOTE:1] from the altar. He came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon told him, “Go home.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “sent and they brought him down.”
Heb “Go to your house.”
